protocol.name: htm_shell_v1
protocol.description:
This protocol assigns an authorized HTMShell controller a semantic shell-root role on an ordinary wl_surface. Surface content, buffers, damage, frame callbacks, output information, and input continue to use standard Wayland protocols.
Version 1 is an experimental feasibility contract. It is not a standard and is not part of wayland-protocols.

interface.name: htm_shell_manager_v1
interface.description:
The manager grants shell-root authority to one authorized client. The authenticate request is a provisional Gate B.0 bootstrap mechanism, not a commitment to a production authentication policy.
A compositor must withhold shell authority until authorization succeeds. Authorization is scoped to the Wayland client connection and disappears when that connection is destroyed.

entry.name: unauthorized
entry.summary: authorization failed or was not completed

entry.name: controller_exists
entry.summary: another client already controls HTMShell roots

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: the surface is invalid or already has a role

entry.name: invalid_output
entry.summary: the output is invalid or unavailable

entry.name: duplicate_root
entry.summary: the surface already owns an HTMShell root

enum.name: capability
enum.description: Capability identifiers describe contract semantics, never compositor implementation details. Unknown values must be ignored by clients.

entry.name: standard_pointer_focus
entry.summary: shell roots participate in normal Wayland pointer targeting

enum.name: role
enum.description: Roles specify desktop semantics rather than a render stage or numeric z-index. Version 1 defines only the role exercised by this feasibility gate.

entry.name: overlay
entry.summary: above ordinary applications and below secure lock content

request.name: authenticate
request.description: The token is an opaque, single-session test capability. A production authorization mechanism may instead restrict global visibility, inherit authority from the compositor, or use session-manager integration.

request.name: get_root
request.description: This request permanently assigns a shell-root role to surface. The role remains attached to the wl_surface for its lifetime, even after the root object is destroyed. The client must not attach a buffer until it has acknowledged the initial configure event.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying this object does not destroy roots already created by this client. Client disconnection always revokes controller authority and destroys all associated roots.

event.name: capability
event.description: This event is sent after successful authorization and before ready.

event.name: ready
event.description: After this event, the client may create roots using advertised roles.

interface.name: htm_shell_root_v1
interface.description: The root owns semantic placement for one wl_surface on one wl_output. The compositor chooses its internal scene placement. The client continues to use wl_surface requests for content and standard seat objects for input.

entry.name: invalid_ack
entry.summary: the configure serial is unknown or stale

entry.name: buffer_before_ack
entry.summary: a buffer was committed before the initial configure ack

entry.name: invalid_size
entry.summary: committed surface dimensions exceed implementation limits

request.name: ack_configure
request.description: The client acknowledges that subsequent surface state is based on this configure. A client must acknowledge the initial configure before attaching its first buffer.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The compositor must immediately remove the root from presentation and input targeting. The wl_surface keeps its permanent role and cannot be reused for an incompatible role.

event.name: configure
event.description: Width and height are output-local logical dimensions. Buffer scale and fractional-scale behavior use existing Wayland protocols.
